title: Presentability of a Cartesian fibration with presentable fibers
statement: Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a Cartesian fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], classified by $G:\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ with fibers $\mathcal E_b$. Assume $\mathcal B$ and every $\mathcal E_b$ are presentable, every Cartesian restriction $G(f):\mathcal E_{b'}\to\mathcal E_b$ is a right adjoint, and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, $G$ carries every small $\kappa$-filtered colimit diagram $b:I\to\mathcal B$ to a limiting cone $G(\operatorname{colim}_I b)\simeq\lim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}G(b_i)$. Then $\mathcal E$ is presentable and $p$ is accessible, meaning that $p$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$. The base and total categories may be large in the smaller universe; their presentability is relative to that smaller universe, with all objects contained in a sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Definition 10.1 and Theorem 10.3, printed pp.29-32, including the proof sentence that establishes accessibility of the projection. This is the v3 numbering (2020); the GH 2015 reference cites its earlier Theorem 9.3. There is no global small-base assumption. Read from retained sandbox source; full shared archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Write $f^*=G(f)$ for $f:b\to b'$ and choose its left adjoint $f_!$. For $x\in\mathcal E_b$, the unit $x\to f^*f_!x$ followed by the Cartesian lift $f^*f_!x\to f_!x$ gives an edge $s:x\to f_!x$ over $f$. We verify that $s$ is cocartesian. For $z$ over $c$, compare $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(f_!x,z)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,c)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b',c)$, by precomposition with $s$. Both spaces lie over the SAME base $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b',c)$. Over $v:b'\to c$, their fibers identify with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_{b'}}(f_!x,v^*z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_b}(x,f^*v^*z)$. These identifications follow by applying the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to the Cartesian lifts of $v$ and $vf$, then taking the fibers over identity arrows at their sources. Under them the comparison is $h\mapsto f^*(h)\eta_x$, exactly the given mapping-space adjunction equivalence. It is natural in $v$ by the coherent classification $G$ and the unit. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] over the identity of that common base. The comparison is an equivalence, so [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] says that $s$ is cocartesian. This gives every cocartesian lift required by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; thus $p$ is also cocartesian, with transport $f_!$.

source.place: Remark 10.2, expanded mapping-space verification of adjoint transports.

proof.text: The base and fibers admit all small colimits by their assumed presentability. Each $f_!$ preserves those colimits because it has right adjoint $f^*$, by [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits]. For a small coherent diagram $e:J\to\mathcal E$, put $b=\operatorname{colim}_J pe$. With base cocone arrows $t_j:pe(j)\to b$, that node constructs its total colimit as $\operatorname{colim}_j t_{j,!}e(j)$ in the fiber over $b$. Hence $\mathcal E$ has all small colimits. Moreover the image of this constructed total colimit cocone under $p$ is exactly the chosen base colimit cocone, so $p$ preserves it. Every other colimit cocone of $e$ is equivalent to this one, and its image remains equivalent to the same base colimit cone. Thus $p$ preserves all small colimits, including the empty one. In particular it preserves small filtered colimits, which already proves its asserted accessibility.

source.place: Lemma 10.7 and first sentence of the proof of Theorem 10.3; projection preservation read directly from the existing colimit formula.

proof.text: Let $\kappa_0$ be the regular cardinal in the hypothesis on $G$, and let $\alpha$ witness accessibility of $\mathcal B$ in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Choose an infinite cardinal $\theta\geq\alpha,\kappa_0$ and put $\kappa=(2^\theta)^+$. Then $\kappa$ is an uncountable regular cardinal, and for $a<\kappa$ and $b<\alpha$ we have $a^b\leq(2^\theta)^\theta=2^\theta<\kappa$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-rank-calculus] to see that $\mathcal B$ is $\kappa$-accessible. A $\kappa$-filtered diagram is also $\kappa_0$-filtered, since every $\kappa_0$-small shape is $\kappa$-small. Thus $G$ still takes these filtered colimits to limits. By [lem-coef-accessible-compact-slice-density], the full category of $\kappa$-compact objects is essentially small; choose a small equivalent full model $i:A\to\mathcal B$. For each $b$, the compact-source slice $A_{/b}$ is essentially small and $\kappa$-filtered, and the canonical diagram $(a,i(a)\to b)\mapsto i(a)$ has colimit $b$. We always replace these slices by small equivalent diagrams before applying the hypothesis on $G$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, first paragraph: choose a compatible cardinal and a small compact base. The cardinal bound and slice presentation are made explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe], small spaces admit all small colimits, and their inclusion into spaces in the containing universe is fully faithful and preserves those colimits. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability], $\mathcal P(A)$ admits all small colimits since $A$ is small. Define $j:\mathcal B\to\mathcal P(A)$ by $j(b)(a)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(i(a),b)$. Compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] says that each mapping-space evaluation preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits in the containing universe. The universe inclusion just cited reflects colimit cocones with small-space apex: restrict their mapping-space universal property to test objects in the fully faithful small-space subcategory. Thus every evaluation of $j$ preserves these colimits in small spaces as well. The pointwise criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore says that $j$ preserves those colimits. Since $i$ is fully faithful, $j(i(a))=y(a)$, the Yoneda presheaf. Applying $j$ to the slice presentation of step 3 gives $j(b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{A_{/b}}y(a)$. The colimit mapping formulas of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and the full Yoneda evaluation equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], applied with its category equal to the small category $A$ and its presheaf equal to $j(c)$, now give, naturally in $b,c$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(A)}(j(b),j(c))\simeq\lim_{A_{/b}^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(i(a),c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,c)$. Thus $j$ is fully faithful and accessible. This establishes the needed presheaf embedding directly, rather than using an uncited assertion about Ind categories.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, presheaf embedding of the compactly generated base; direct density proof of the portion needed here.

proof.text: The restriction $H=G\circ i^{\mathrm{op}}$ is indexed by the small infinity category $A^{\mathrm{op}}$, has presentable values, and has right adjoint arrows by the hypotheses on $G$. Apply [lem-coef-small-right-adjoint-diagram-compact-model]. It supplies one uncountable regular $\lambda$ and a coherent functor $F_0:A\to\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ with a natural equivalence $H\simeq\operatorname{Ind}^{\mathrm R}_\lambda F_0^{\mathrm{op}}$. This changes the size of the compact fibers, not the variance: $F_0(f)$ extends to the left adjoint transport and its right adjoint is $G(i(f))$. The smallness used here is only smallness of $A$, not of the original base $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, final paragraph: the uniform lambda and the compact-object diagram.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-ind-presheaf-fibration-accessibility] to $A$, $\lambda$ and $F_0$ from step 5. Its hypotheses are exactly that $A$ and each $F_0(a)$ are small, the fibers admit $\lambda$-small colimits and the arrows preserve these. The lemma gives a limit extension $\widehat G:\mathcal P(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of $H$. Apply the opposite of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] in a containing universe to obtain its Cartesian unstraightening $\widehat p:\widehat{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal P(A)$. The presheaf-fibration lemma now says that this total category and projection are accessible. The base $\mathcal P(A)$ is presentable by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability], since $A$ is small in the original universe. Thus every category in the pullback argument below is accessible in that same universe; enlarging the containing universe only accommodates their collections of objects.

source.place: Proposition 10.5 and the final paragraph of the proof of Theorem 10.3.

proof.text: We identify the pullback along $j$ explicitly. In the category-of-elements formula of [lem-coef-ind-presheaf-fibration-accessibility], take $X=j(b)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] with its category equal to $A$ and its presheaf equal to $j(b)$. Its universe and local-smallness hypotheses hold because $A$ is small in the original universe and $j(b)$ is small-space-valued. By its full Yoneda evaluation equivalence, a map $y(a)\to j(b)$ is a point of $j(b)(a)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(i(a),b)$, with the same coherent triangles and higher homotopies. Its element category is therefore the compact-source slice $A_{/b}$ from step 3. There is a canonical comparison $G(b)\to\widehat G(j(b))\simeq\lim_{A_{/b}^{\mathrm{op}}}G(i(a))$ induced by the arrows $i(a)\to b$. It is an equivalence: the slice is small after replacement, is $\kappa$-filtered, and has colimit $b$, so the hypothesis on $G$ applies. The comparisons are natural in $b$: a map $b\to c$ postcomposes every arrow $i(a)\to b$, and contravariance of $G$ identifies its two induced cone maps by composition; the coherent classification retains all these homotopies. Hence $G\simeq\widehat G\circ j^{\mathrm{op}}$ as coherent functors. Apply the opposite of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] in a containing universe: its classification and base-change compatibility identify the given $\mathcal E$ over $\mathcal B$ with the infinity-categorical pullback $\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal P(A)}\widehat{\mathcal E}$. No pullback over a globally small $\mathcal B$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, pullback square; the comparison cone and its variance are written explicitly.

proof.text: The two functors into $\mathcal P(A)$ are accessible: $j$ by step 4 and $\widehat p$ by step 6. Their sources are accessible: $\mathcal B$ by assumption and $\widehat{\mathcal E}$ by step 6; the target is accessible by its presheaf presentability. Thus [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] applies to the pullback identified in step 7 and makes $\mathcal E$ accessible. Together with all small colimits from step 2, this is presentability by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. The projection is accessible by the explicit colimit calculation in step 2, so no stronger functorial conclusion than the statement of the pullback node has been used.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, application of HTT Proposition 5.4.6.6 and conclusion.
